title: Special Council - August 14, 2025

items.title: Call to Order
notes: Regional Chair K. Redman called the meeting to order at 8:30 a.m.

items.title: Land Acknowledgement
notes: Regional Chair K. Redman provided a land acknowledgement.

items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
notes: None declared.

items.title: Jey Legarie
notes: Jey Legarie, Waterloo, addressed Regional Council on how they can positively impact the community if appointed as Regional Councillor.

items.title: Asma'a Al-Wahsh
notes: Asma'a Al-Wahsh, Waterloo, addressed Regional Council on how they can best serve the Region of Waterloo. They noted that if they were appointed, they would work in collaboration with current Council. and would prioritize transit, childcare, and sustainability.

items.title: Marinus de Groot
notes: Marinus de Groot, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on the initiatives that they would prioritize, specifically, the importance of funding arts and heritage throughout the community. They explained how their experience on the Arts Fund has given them municipal knowledge that would be applicable in their role as a Regional Councillor.

attachments.name: Marinus de Groot Personal Statement of Qualifications.pdf

items.title: Piyush Nanda
notes: Piyush Nanda, Cambridge, addressed Regional Council on why they are seeking appointment to Regional Council. They explained that they want to be a Regional Councillor to help the community by listening to residents. They highlighted that their varying skill set would be an asset to Regional Council such as their analytical and language skills.

attachments.name: Piyush Nanda Region of Waterloo Councillor Resume.pdf

items.title: Brooklin Wallis
notes: Brooklin Wallis, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on the reason they should be appointed as a Councillor. She highlighted their community commitments and that she has ran in previous elections with the support of approximately 4000 votes. She further highlighted that she would provide a diverse perspective as she is under 30, rents, uses transit, and is a cyclist.

items.title: Julie Kalbfleisch
notes: Julie Kalbfleisch, Waterloo, addressed Regional Council on their previous experience in Municipal government and their community involvement. They explained that their approach would balance urban and rural priorities.

attachments.name: Personal Statement of Qualifications - Regional Councillor Appointment.pdf

items.title: Michael Filion
notes: Did not appear when called.

items.title: Christina Schipper
notes: Christina Schipper, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on their priorities if they were to be appointed as a Councillor. They highlighted the issues that the Region of Waterloo is encountering and how their experiences as a teacher have provided insight on how to help those most disadvantaged in the community.

items.title: Fauzia Mazhar
notes: Fauzia Mazhar, Waterloo, addressed Regional Council on their community engagement and civic participation. They highlighted that they have prioritized municipal government and will continue to champion affordable housing and homelessness prevention. They noted that in the 2018 municipal election they received approximately 10,000 votes. They expressed the importance of appointing a Councillor with an inclusive and experienced voice.

items.title: Simon Guthrie
notes: Simon Guthrie, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on their commitments to the community if they were to be appointed as a Councillor.

items.title: Carrie Wright
notes: Carrie Wright, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on their connection to the Region of Waterloo and their commitment to the community. They noted that their interest aligns with the Regional Strategic Plan specifically growth and sustainability.

items.title: Mifrah Abid
notes: Mifrah Abid, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on the importance of providing all residents with care and respect. They explained that the Region of Waterloo is their chosen home that they have invested in and wish to serve the community by being a conduit between residents that have lived in the Region their whole lives and those that are newcomers to the area. They further explained that they are passionate about community involvement and would be an asset as a Regional Councillor.

items.title: Allan Beaupre
notes: Allan Beaupre, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on the importance of being fiscally responsible and how he can assist with providing a realistic perspective to Council on these matters.

items.title: Brad Ball
notes: Brad Ball, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on why Regional Council should appoint them as a Councillor. They provided a brief overview of their background that includes both agriculture and technology and noted their involvement with various local organizations including Conestoga College.

attachments.name: Brad Ball Backgrounder and Statement of Interest.pdf

items.title: Shannon Knelsen
notes: Shannon Knelsen, Cambridge, addressed Regional Council on how their lived experiences would be an asset as a Regional Councillor. They expressed their dedication for ensuring that the services that were available to them in their youth continue to be available to the community in the future. They noted that their priorities are to provide services to youth, seniors, and those experiencing homelessness.

items.title: Christopher (Chris) Moser
notes: Chris Moser, Waterloo, addressed Regional Council on the reasons they should be appointed as a Councillor. They stated that their priorities include taxes and affordable housing.

items.title: Hanan Wahib
notes: Hanan Wahib, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on their involvement with community projects such as the Iron Horse Trail and volunteering for the newcomer program at the YMCA.

items.title: Peter Eglin
notes: Peter Eglin, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on their priorities for the community including affordable housing and preservation of agriculture.

attachments.name: Application for Appointment to Region of Waterloo Council.pdf

items.title: Maggie Lam
notes: Maggie Lam, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council by providing a brief overview of their professional background and highlights of their public service which includes being the Chair of the Public Art Advisory Committee. They emphasized the importance of the rural and natural area throughout the Region. They further emphasized that if appointed as Regional Councillor they will move business forward to align with the establish strategic plan and bring a unifying, but different perspective to Council.

items.title: Wazhma Frogh
notes: Wazhma Frogh, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on why they should be appointed as a Regional Councillor. They highlighted their career accomplishments as a human rights lawyer as well as their participation in community initiatives such as the Coalition of Muslim Women. They noted that their priorities will include investing in a safe community which includes affordable housing, culturally responsive mental health supports, and inclusive and accessible transit.

items.title: Philip Molto
notes: Philip Molto, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on their qualifications to be appointed as a Regional Councillor. They described their deep roots in the community which include raising a family locally and their ongoing volunteerism. He noted that he ran for Regional Council in 2018 and has been involved in various elections.

items.title: Kevin White
notes: Kevin White, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on the importance of creating inclusive spaces and meaningful support services throughout the community. They noted that they are a supporter of the arts and libraries. They highlighted that their intention as a Councillor would be to ensure that all decisions by Regional Council would align with the Regional Strategic Plan.

attachments.name: Region of Waterloo Kevin White Statement of Qualifications.pdf

items.title: Ayad Kamal
notes: Ayad Kamal, Waterloo, addressed Regional Council on the issues that the community is encountering in the Region of waterloo. They expressed concern for various issues that Regional Council is facing and will continue to face in the coming years. They emphasized that as a Regional Councillor they would be able assist in both identifying and mitigating risk.

items.title: David Shen
notes:
David Shen, Waterloo, addressed Regional Council on why they should be appointed as a Regional Councillor. They confirmed that they would not plan to run for re-election in the 2026 Ontario Municipal election as they consider this appointment as an interim position. They highlighted that their priorities would include the budget process, Regional Strategic Plan, and adhering to the Regional Code of Conduct. 

The meeting was recessed at 10:31 a.m.

items.title: Ronald Green
notes:
The meeting resumed at 10:46 a.m.

Ronald Green, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on why they should be appointed as a Councillor. They explained that they have worked in both the private and public sectors and in various communities and countries. They explained that a singular decision can have a wide-ranging impact to various areas, and their analytical skills would be an asset on Regional Council to make these important decisions.

items.title: Sam Nabi
notes: Sam Nabi, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on seeking the position of Regional Councillor. They highlighted that they are a local small business owner, a musician, and a community organizer. They have led various community roundtables that brought individuals together for collaboration and discussion. Their business has also prioritized sustainability and accessibility.

items.title: Julie Hall
notes: Julie Hall, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on their various accomplishments throughout the community. They provided a brief overview of applicable skills and experiences that could be beneficial as a Regional Councillor.

attachments.name: Julie Hall - Regional Council statement + CV_Redacted.pdf

items.title: Marcus Drasdo
notes: Marcus Drasdo, Waterloo, addressed Regional Council on various life experiences that would assist them in being an effective Regional Council. They summarized their community involvement including organizing an annual Terry Fox Run.

items.title: Graham Edwards
notes: Graham Edwards, Cambridge, addressed Regional Council on why they would a good Candidate to serve as a Regional Councillor. They spoke about the immense responsibility that Regional Council holds on the daily lives of residents and why it's so critical to have a diverse range of experiences and voices on Regional Council. They emphasized that their lived experience of being an immigrant to Canada provides them with a perspective that should be represented on Council.

attachments.name: Graham Edwards_Personal Statement of Interest and Qualifications for Regional Councillor.pdf

items.title: Gordon Greavette
notes: Gordon Greavette, Waterloo, addressed Regional Council and requested their support to be appointed as a Councillor. They provided a brief overview of their community and work experiences, specifically, they noted their participation on the Grand River Conservation Authority as a citizen appointee. He noted that he is an active resident of the Region of Waterloo and all its area municipalities.

items.title: Brian Bourke
notes: Brian Bourke, Waterloo, addressed Regional Council on the importance of innovation whilst continuing to be cautious. They emphasized that the position of Regional Councillor is difficult and can take time to learn. They further emphasized that their goal, if appointed as Councillor, would be to try to do good works and continue to make a welcoming community to build a life in.

attachments.name: Brian Bourke - Personal Statement of Interest and Qualifications.pdf

items.title: Douglas Dutchak
notes: Douglas Dutchak, Wellesley, addressed on Regional Council on the reasons why they should be appointed to Council. They provided a brief overview of their personal and professional background. They emphasized the importance of "showing up" and how they have been a dedicated worker and father for over 45 years and that they will be dedicated to serving on Regional Council if appointed.

attachments.name: Application of Doug Dutchak for the Region of Waterloo Council Vacancy 2.pdf

items.title: John Champion
notes: John Champion, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on the reasons they applied to fill the Councillor vacancy. They highlighted that they are passionate about donating blood to help those in need, mentoring youth, and Veteran services. They have worked both of the Canadian Military and Region of Waterloo Police Services. They further highlighted that they would be an asset on Regional Council as they are great in a crisis.

items.title: David Guerin
notes: David Guerin, Cambridge, addressed Regional Council on their community involvement and how that may be an asset to serve as a Councillor. They provided a brief overview of various instances in which they provided assistance to disadvantaged individuals.

attachments.name: David Guerin - Application for Council Vacancy 2025 07 31.pdf

items.title: Michael Beauchemin
notes: Michael Beauchemin, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on the reasons why they should be appointed as a Councillor. They highlighted that they have been involved in the Region since moving to the Region for their undergraduate degree. They further highlighted that they are a quick learner and have experience being on various Committees and Boards.

items.title: Jesse Rodgers
notes: Jesse Rodgers, Wilmot, addressed Regional Council on why they should be appointed on Council.  They emphasized the importance of preservation while encouraging both sustainable growth and business opportunities.

attachments.name: Statement of Qualifications for Regional Councillor - Jesse Rodgers.pdf

items.title: Matthew Ichim
notes: Matthew Ichim, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on their prioritizations if they were appointed as a Councillor. Their primary priority is chronic homelessness while balancing the concerns of increasing property taxes. They noted their previous work in the public sector and running in a previous election for a Regional Councillor seat.

items.title: John Roe
notes: John Roe, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on seeking support to be appointed as a Councillor. They have worked in journalism, education, and as a volunteer working with refugees. They provided a brief overview of their priorities which include increasing housing construction and overall affordability.

attachments.name: John Roe - Statement of Qualifications and Interest.pdf

items.title: Jonathan Massimi
notes:
Jonathan Massimi, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council 

Manager of community development for United Way - participated in grassroots neighbourhood initiatives including a mental health program and alternatives to police interventions during the Covid-19 pandemic.

items.title: Hin Tat Lam
notes: H.T. Lam, Waterloo, addressed Regional Council on seeking the position as a Councillor. They highlighted their priorities which include strategic housing, environmental leadership through infrastructure designs, transit that promotes sustainable growth, and regain Regional planning authority to ensure water and farmland preservation. They further highlighted the impact that Regional Council has on the community.

items.title: Prakash Venkataraman
notes: Prakash Venkataraman, Cambridge, addressed Regional Councillor on their public service including their involvement on the Chamber of Commerce. They emphasized the importance of proper representation on Council to ensure that there is a voice for those that are disadvantaged.

items.title: Vishal Chaudhary
notes: Vishal Chaudhary, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on how they would benefit the community if appointed as a Councillor. They highlighted the importance of continued growth as change is inevitable, so it is important for Council to lead the change instead of follow.

items.title: Joseph Gowing
notes: Joseph Gowing, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on the value of participating in the community including municipal government and local businesses. He emphasized the importance of having a genuine understanding of the diverse needs across the Region and that his experiences living in both Cambridge and Kitchener has given him that understanding. He also has public service experience as working on the Waterloo Catholic District School Board as a school board trustee. He further emphasized the importance of local businesses and community leadership. He will prioritize housing and homelessness, transportation development, and providing support for both rural and urban communities.

items.title: Ruthann Fisher
notes:
Ruthann Fisher, Kitchener, addressed Regional Council on the priorities they would focus on as a Regional Councillor. The priorities include climate change, childcare, senior assistance, and individuals with disabilities.

The meeting was recessed at 12:28 p.m.

items.title: Correspondence
notes:
The meeting resumed at 12:39 p.m.

Received for information.

items.title: Applicant Election
notes: Tim Brubacher, Acting Director Council and Administrative Services/Regional Clerk, indicated that there was a three-way tie between F. Mazhar, C. Wright, and M. Lam. He explained that since the remaining candidate J. Gowing did not have a majority vote that one of the candidates involved in the three-way tie would need to be eliminated by drawn lot. The three candidates’ names were placed into a box and T. Brubacher pulled C. Wright’s name from the box for elimination.
